The 39-page strategy, posted November 10, 2025 and read in full, has five pillars, gives [portfolio acquisition executives](#term:pae) "expanded authorities for resourcing, requirements, and acquisition decisions within prescribed portfolios" (p. 15), directs [OT](#term:other-transaction) authority "for prototype and [follow-on production](#term:follow-on-production) efforts where in the best interest of the warfighter and the taxpayer" (p. 10), keeps [MTA](#term:middle-tier-of-acquisition) while eliminating its Advisory Boards (p. 20), and proposes portfolio [scorecards](#term:goals) (p. 21) [1264](#cite:1264).

A third-party-hosted copy or digest reports implementing guidance in 30 days, Military Department [PAE](#term:pae) implementation plans in 60 days, commercial-first guidance in 90 days and other reforms in 180 days, with PAE terms of four years and a possible two-year extension [1265](#cite:1265). Law-firm digests give differing day counts [1266](#cite:1266) [1267](#cite:1267) [1269](#cite:1269) [1270](#cite:1270). None is confirmed against the memo.

[GSA](#term:gsa) [Class Deviation](#term:class-deviation) RFO-2025-FSS-GSAR 538, issued August 13, 2025 and effective November 3, 2025, relocates [Federal Supply Schedule](#term:mas) ordering procedures from [FAR](#term:far) subpart 8.4 to [GSAR](#term:gsar) subpart 538.71, retaining the requirement to seek at least three quotes above the [micro-purchase threshold](#term:micro-purchase-threshold) and the consideration of small businesses [503](#cite:503). GSA's buyer page gives GSAR subpart 538.71 as the home of ordering and [BPA](#term:bpa) procedures [504](#cite:504); the overhaul Part 8 model text points to subpart 538.71 [522](#cite:522); MAS Refresh 30 (November 2025) added a statement directing users to gsa.gov for the procedures [486](#cite:486). Codified FAR 8.405-5, where order [set-asides](#term:set-aside) are at the ordering [contracting officer](#term:contracting-officer)'s discretion, remains in the Code [502](#cite:502). In rulemaking: FAR Case 2026-003 (proposed September 18, 2026) would codify the overhaul of Part 8 [521](#cite:521), and a GSAR [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) on Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures ([FR](#term:federal-register) Doc. 2026-19331, September 22, 2026) appears in the Federal Register search [407](#cite:407).

[Final rule](#term:final-rule) 90 [FR](#term:federal-register) 41872 ([FAR](#term:far) Case 2024-001, [FAC](#term:fac) 2025-06), published August 27, 2025 and effective October 1, 2025, raised the [micro-purchase threshold](#term:micro-purchase-threshold) from $10,000 to $15,000; the [simplified acquisition threshold](#term:simplified-acquisition-threshold) from $250,000 to $350,000; the commercial [simplified procedures](#term:simplified-acquisition-procedures) ceiling (FAR 13.500) from $7,500,000 to $9,000,000; the [subcontracting plan](#term:subcontracting-plan) threshold from $750,000 to $900,000 (construction $1,500,000 to $2,000,000); the [8(a)](#term:eight-a) [sole-source](#term:sole-source) justification threshold (FAR 6.204) from $25,000,000 to $30,000,000; and [certified cost or pricing data](#term:certified-cost-or-pricing-data) from $2,000,000 to $2,500,000 [340](#cite:340) [417](#cite:417). Not adjusted: [Construction Wage Rate Requirements](#term:davis-bacon), [Service Contract Labor Standards](#term:service-contract-act), [performance and payment bonds](#term:miller-act), and [trade agreements](#term:buy-american) thresholds [340](#cite:340). Official text that lags: 13 [CFR](#term:cfr) 125.3 still prints $750,000 and $1,500,000 for subcontracting plans [704](#cite:704). Later statute: 10 [U.S.C.](#term:usc) 3702 reads $10,000,000 for prime contracts entered after June 30, 2026 (see chg-ndaa-fy26-1804-tina) [1036](#cite:1036).

[SBIR](#term:sbir)/[STTR](#term:sttr) authority lapsed: 15 [U.S.C.](#term:usc) 638(m) in the 2024 edition ends the authorization on September 30, 2025 [3](#cite:3), and [NIH](#term:agency-abbreviations) states the legislative authority "expired on October 1, 2025" [27](#cite:27). On November 17, 2025 NIH expired all 24 listed SBIR/STTR funding opportunities and said it would issue no noncompeting continuation awards until reauthorization [27](#cite:27). [CRS](#term:crs) describes a six-month lapse [59](#cite:59). The lapse ended with [Pub. L. 119-83](#term:sbir-reauthorization-2026) on April 13, 2026 (see chg-pl-119-83-reauthorization) [1](#cite:1).

[RFO](#term:revolutionary-far-overhaul) [Part 19](#term:far-part-19) [model deviation text](#term:class-deviation) was issued September 26, 2025 [391](#cite:391). [GSA](#term:gsa) adopted it by Class Deviation RFO-2025-19, issued September 26, 2025 and effective November 3, 2025, in effect until rescinded or incorporated into the [FAR](#term:far) [400](#cite:400). DoD adopted it by Class Deviation 2026-O0037 (dated 21 January 2026 on DoD's index), effective February 1, 2026, with a deviation [DFARS](#term:dfars) Part 219; under it an [8(a)](#term:eight-a) contract "may be awarded directly to the 8(a) participant; an [SBA](#term:sba) signature on the contract is not required." [401](#cite:401) [402](#cite:402) The model text states the total [set-aside](#term:set-aside) rule once at 19.104-1, makes order set-asides permissive at 19.111-2, keeps [sole-source](#term:sole-source) caps of $8.5 million / $5.5 million ([HUBZone](#term:hubzone), [WOSB](#term:wosb)/EDWOSB, and the 8(a) competition threshold) and $8.5 million / $5 million ([SDVOSB](#term:sdvosb)), and requires a [subcontracting plan](#term:subcontracting-plan) above $900,000 ($2 million for construction of a public facility) at 19.109 [391](#cite:391). No Part 19 [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) had been published as of October 3, 2026 [407](#cite:407).

NavalX was folded into the Naval Rapid Capabilities Office in August 2025; the office consolidates NavalX, the Disruptive Capabilities Office, the Maritime Accelerated Response Capability Cell and Replicator activities, with Tech Bridges among its focus areas [1280](#cite:1280).

Phase one of the [FAR overhaul](#term:revolutionary-far-overhaul): the [FAR Council](#term:far-council) released [model deviation text](#term:class-deviation) part by part, beginning with Part 1 on May 2, 2025 (updated March 16, 2026); Parts 4 and 12 on August 14, 2025; Part 5 on August 8, 2025; Part 9 on August 21, 2025; Part 7 on September 4, 2025; [Part 13](#term:simplified-acquisition-procedures) on September 18, 2025; [Part 15](#term:far-part-15) on September 30, 2025 [389](#cite:389). The acquisition university's log records the September 30, 2025 release (Parts 15, 16, 22, 23, 25, 32, 42 and 53) as completing all parts, and a November 7, 2025 release of all model text with [FAR](#term:far) Companion 2.0 [410](#cite:410). Model text for Parts 1, 5, 10, 22, 25 and 52 was updated March 16, 2026 for the [trade agreements](#term:buy-american) thresholds [final rule](#term:final-rule) (FAR Case 2025-007), effective March 13, 2026 [575](#cite:575). Each agency adopts the text by its own class deviation; the codified FAR stands at [FAC](#term:fac) 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026 [418](#cite:418).

[Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement, was signed April 15, 2025 and published April 18, 2025 ([FR](#term:federal-register) Doc. 2025-06839) [386](#cite:386). Section 4 directs that the [FAR](#term:far) be amended within 180 days so that it contains only provisions required by statute or otherwise necessary; section 6 has retained non-statutory provisions expire 4 years after the [final rule](#term:final-rule)'s effective date unless renewed by the [FAR Council](#term:far-council) [386](#cite:386). OMB Memorandum M-25-26 set two phases: model [class deviations](#term:class-deviation), then rulemaking [403](#cite:403).

[Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14265, Modernizing Defense Acquisitions and Spurring Innovation in the Defense Industrial Base, was signed April 9, 2025 and published April 15, 2025 (90 [FR](#term:federal-register) 15621) [1262](#cite:1262). It set a reform plan due within 60 days (Sec. 3), an MDAP review within 90 days with programs more than 15% behind schedule or over cost considered for cancellation (Sec. 6), and a workforce plan within 120 days, including field training teams (Sec. 5) [1262](#cite:1262).

[Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14240, Eliminating Waste and Saving Taxpayer Dollars by Consolidating Procurement, signed March 20, 2025 (90 [FR](#term:federal-register) 13671), directs consolidation of domestic procurement of common goods and services in [GSA](#term:gsa): agency heads submit proposals within 60 days, the Administrator submits a comprehensive plan within 90 days, and "the Director of [OMB](#term:far-council) shall designate the Administrator as the executive agent for all Government-wide acquisition contracts for information technology" [509](#cite:509). OMB M-25-31 (July 18, 2025) calls for [model deviation text](#term:class-deviation) mandating use of existing governmentwide contracts [510](#cite:510). Neither document mentions small business in the text fetched [509](#cite:509) [510](#cite:510). What GSA itself says: small business goal credit follows the funding agency [513](#cite:513), and on OneGov "OEMs serving as [primes](#term:prime-and-subcontractor) will be required to demonstrate meaningful subcontracting and partnering opportunities with small businesses, consistent with federal small business goals." [519](#cite:519) References 510 and 513 were not re-read in the recheck pass.

The Secretary's memo "Directing Modern [Software Acquisition](#term:software-acquisition-pathway) to Maximize Lethality" is dated March 6, 2025 on the Software Acquisition pathway page [1252](#cite:1252). The November 2025 strategy restates it as making [CSOs](#term:cso) and [OTs](#term:other-transaction) "the default [solicitation](#term:solicitation) and award approaches for acquiring capabilities under the SWP" (p. 2) [1264](#cite:1264), and [DIU](#term:diu)'s account of it is dated March 7, 2025 [1255](#cite:1255). The memo PDF returned 403 and was not read.

[SBA](#term:sba)'s release of February 24, 2025 states: "SBA has returned the [8(a)](#term:eight-a) [SDB](#term:sdb) contracting goal to its statutory level of 5%." [317](#cite:317) The same release says the previous Administration had raised the goal to 15% [317](#cite:317). The statutory floor for [socially and economically disadvantaged](#term:disadvantage) firms is not less than 5 percent [374](#cite:374). SECONDARY ONLY for the date of the reset: two sources put the [FY2025](#term:fiscal-year) goal change at January 24, 2025 [377](#cite:377) [380](#cite:380).

[DFARS](#term:dfars) Case 2019-D043, [final rule](#term:final-rule) published December 18, 2024 and effective January 17, 2025, replaced the extendable 5-year [protection period](#term:sbir-data-rights) with "a single, non-extendable 20-year period" followed by perpetual government purpose rights, and added provision 252.227-7040 and [clause](#term:clause-numbering) 252.227-7041 for [STTR](#term:sttr) intellectual-property allocation [233](#cite:233). DFARS 252.227-7018 (AUG 2025) runs the protection period 20 years from contract award [24](#cite:24). Official text that lags: [FAR](#term:far) 52.227-20 (May 2014) still gives 4 years [25](#cite:25); FAR Case 2020-010, proposed April 7, 2023, would change it to 20 years, and no final rule was found as of 2026-10-03 [228](#cite:228).

[NSF](#term:agency-abbreviations) Translation to Practice (NSF 25-540) succeeded Partnerships for Innovation; the PFI [solicitation](#term:solicitation) NSF 23-538 is archived [1401](#cite:1401) [1402](#cite:1402). The first TTP-T and TTP-P deadline was November 18, 2025 [1401](#cite:1401).

On December 11, 2024 the FTC and DOJ withdrew the Guidelines for Collaboration Among Competitors (vote 3-2), saying they "no longer provide reliable guidance about how enforcers assess the legality of collaborations involving competitors." [828](#cite:828) On February 23, 2026 the two agencies sought public comment toward guidance on business collaborations (docket ATR-2026-0001; comments were due April 24, 2026); the listed topics do not name government-contract [teaming](#term:teaming-agreement) and no replacement guidance was found [829](#cite:829). Offerors still certify independent pricing under [FAR](#term:far) 52.203-2 [765](#cite:765).

[DHS](#term:agency-abbreviations)'s [other transaction authority](#term:other-transaction) at 6 [U.S.C.](#term:usc) 391 shows, in the text as displayed, a sunset of September 30, 2024 [1352](#cite:1352). A Senate committee report says the authority "expired on September 30, 2024" and that S. 4024 would extend it through [fiscal year](#term:fiscal-year) 2027 [1353](#cite:1353). No enacted extension was found in the sweep, so the status recorded is that of the proposed extension.

[ARPA-H](#term:arpa-h) announced four Mission Office Innovative Solutions Openings on March 15, 2024: "Awards made from each Mission Office ISO will generally be in the form of [other transactions](#term:other-transaction)." [1382](#cite:1382) Per the sweep's summary of the announcement they replaced the agency-wide Open [BAA](#term:baa) [1382](#cite:1382), which had been announced March 15, 2023 [1383](#cite:1383).
